questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly represents the five stages of the nursing process?

choices.text: Assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation
Diagnosis, assessment, implementation, planning and evaluation
Planning, assessment, diagnosis, evaluation and implementation
Assessment, planning, implementation, diagnosis and evaluation

questions.rationale: The nursing process follows the systematic sequence of assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation (ADPIE). This framework ensures that psychiatric nursing care is individualised, evidence-based and directed towards achieving measurable patient outcomes.

distractor_rationales.B: Diagnosis cannot appropriately precede the collection and analysis of assessment data.
distractor_rationales.C: Planning cannot be properly undertaken before assessment and nursing diagnosis.
distractor_rationales.D: Nursing diagnosis must precede the development and implementation of the care plan.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old patient is admitted to a psychiatric unit in Ghana because of persistent auditory hallucinations. During assessment, the patient reports hearing voices commanding him to jump from a building. What should the nurse assess FIRST?

choices.text: The patient's educational background
The patient's employment history
The content of the voices, suicidal intent, access to means and immediate safety
The patient's preferred recreational activities

questions.rationale: Command hallucinations involving potentially fatal actions indicate an immediate risk of self-harm. The nurse must assess the content, frequency, perceived authority of the voices, intention to obey them and access to means while implementing appropriate safety precautions.

distractor_rationales.A: Educational history is relevant to comprehensive assessment but does not address the immediate safety threat.
distractor_rationales.B: Employment history does not establish the patient's immediate suicide risk.
distractor_rationales.D: Recreational preferences are not the priority when the patient reports potentially life-threatening command hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a measurable expected outcome in a psychiatric nursing care plan?

choices.text: The patient will become completely normal
The patient will understand everything about mental illness
The patient will improve emotionally
The patient will identify three coping strategies before discharge

questions.rationale: A good expected outcome should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. Identifying three coping strategies provides an observable indicator that can be evaluated during psychiatric nursing care.

distractor_rationales.A: Becoming completely normal is vague and does not provide a measurable clinical outcome.
distractor_rationales.B: Understanding everything is unrealistic and cannot be objectively evaluated.
distractor_rationales.C: Improving emotionally does not specify an observable measure of progress.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse assesses a patient who avoids social interaction, expresses feelings of worthlessness and refuses to participate in group activities. Which nursing diagnosis is MOST appropriate based on these findings?

choices.text: Impaired social interaction
Impaired physical mobility
Risk for impaired skin integrity
Deficient fluid volume

questions.rationale: The patient's withdrawal from social activities and avoidance of interpersonal relationships support the nursing diagnosis of impaired social interaction. Further assessment should establish contributing factors, including depressive symptoms, anxiety and low self-esteem.

distractor_rationales.B: The findings do not indicate limitations in physical movement.
distractor_rationales.C: There is no evidence of an increased risk of skin breakdown in the scenario.
distractor_rationales.D: The patient has no reported findings suggesting dehydration or fluid loss.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of critical thinking in psychiatric nursing?

choices.text: To follow every instruction without questioning its appropriateness
To make evidence-based clinical decisions using assessment findings and professional judgement
To replace clinical guidelines with personal opinions
To avoid involving patients in treatment decisions

questions.rationale: Critical thinking involves analysing clinical information, evaluating evidence and making appropriate nursing decisions. In psychiatric practice, it supports accurate risk assessment, therapeutic interventions and individualised patient care.

distractor_rationales.A: Blindly following instructions without professional judgement can compromise patient safety.
distractor_rationales.C: Personal opinions should not replace evidence-based clinical guidelines.
distractor_rationales.D: Critical thinking supports patient participation rather than excluding patients from decisions.

questions.question_text: A patient diagnosed with schizophrenia frequently refuses prescribed antipsychotic medication because of unpleasant side effects. Which nursing intervention is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Threaten the patient with discharge if medication is refused
Hide the medication inside the patient's food
Explore the patient's concerns, assess side effects and collaborate on an appropriate treatment plan
Discontinue all treatment without consulting the prescriber

questions.rationale: Exploring medication concerns helps identify adverse effects, misconceptions and barriers to treatment adherence. The nurse should communicate findings to the prescriber and support shared decision-making while respecting the patient's rights and applicable mental health legislation.

distractor_rationales.A: Threatening the patient damages the therapeutic relationship and does not address the reason for refusal.
distractor_rationales.B: Concealing medication without lawful authority and appropriate safeguards violates patient autonomy and medication safety.
distractor_rationales.D: The nurse should not independently discontinue prescribed psychiatric treatment.

questions.question_text: During the evaluation stage of the nursing process, a psychiatric nurse discovers that a patient's anxiety has not reduced despite several interventions. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Continue the same interventions indefinitely
Discharge the patient immediately
Ignore the patient's reported anxiety
Reassess the patient and modify the nursing care plan according to the findings

questions.rationale: Evaluation determines whether planned nursing interventions have achieved their expected outcomes. When outcomes are not achieved, the nurse must reassess the patient, identify barriers and revise the care plan appropriately.

distractor_rationales.A: Continuing ineffective interventions without reassessment may delay recovery.
distractor_rationales.B: Failure to achieve an outcome does not automatically justify discharge.
distractor_rationales.C: Ignoring persistent anxiety violates the principles of patient-centred nursing care.

questions.question_text: A patient admitted with depression tells the nurse, 'My family would be better off without me.' Which response demonstrates appropriate clinical reasoning?

choices.text: You should stop thinking negatively
Are you thinking about killing yourself or ending your life?
Your family will be disappointed if you do anything harmful
Let us discuss your childhood experiences instead

questions.rationale: The statement may indicate suicidal ideation and requires direct, non-judgemental suicide risk assessment. Asking explicitly about suicidal thoughts, plans, intentions and access to means helps identify immediate danger and guide appropriate safety interventions.

distractor_rationales.A: Telling the patient to stop thinking negatively dismisses the emotional distress and does not assess suicide risk.
distractor_rationales.C: Using guilt may increase emotional distress and discourage honest disclosure.
distractor_rationales.D: Exploring childhood experiences does not address the immediate possibility of suicide.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is caring for four patients. Which patient should the nurse assess FIRST?

choices.text: A patient with anxiety requesting relaxation exercises
A patient with schizophrenia who refuses to attend group therapy
A patient with depression who has concealed a sharp object and expresses an intention to die
A patient requesting assistance with personal hygiene

questions.rationale: The patient has expressed suicidal intent and possesses a potential means of self-harm, indicating an immediate life-threatening risk. The nurse must initiate appropriate safety precautions, maintain observation and obtain urgent psychiatric assessment.

distractor_rationales.A: Anxiety requires attention but does not present the same immediate danger as an active suicide threat.
distractor_rationales.B: Refusal to participate in group therapy is not automatically an emergency.
distractor_rationales.D: Personal hygiene assistance is important but can wait until the immediate safety threat is addressed.

questions.question_text: A patient reports hearing voices, but the nurse cannot observe the voices directly. What is the MOST appropriate nursing approach?

choices.text: Document the patient's report and assess the characteristics and effect of the hallucinations
Tell the patient that the voices do not exist
Ignore the report because hallucinations cannot be physically observed
Immediately assume that the patient is violent

questions.rationale: Hallucinations are subjective perceptual experiences and must be assessed through the patient's description and observed behaviour. The nurse should document the sensory modality, content, frequency, emotional response and associated safety risks without reinforcing the hallucination.

distractor_rationales.B: Directly arguing about the patient's perception may damage therapeutic communication.
distractor_rationales.C: Hallucinations are clinically significant even when they cannot be directly observed.
distractor_rationales.D: Hallucinations do not automatically mean that a patient is violent.

questions.question_text: A patient with alcohol use disorder has been admitted following repeated withdrawal episodes. Which nursing outcome is MOST appropriate for the immediate care plan?

choices.text: The patient will never consume alcohol again
The patient will independently manage every aspect of recovery within one day
The patient will remain free from withdrawal complications during the immediate observation period
The patient will immediately resume normal occupational activities

questions.rationale: Preventing acute withdrawal complications is an appropriate immediate outcome because alcohol withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium tremens. The nurse should monitor vital signs, consciousness and withdrawal symptoms while administering prescribed treatment.

distractor_rationales.A: Permanent abstinence is a long-term recovery goal rather than an immediate measurable outcome.
distractor_rationales.B: Complete independent recovery within one day is unrealistic.
distractor_rationales.D: Returning to occupational activities is not the immediate priority during acute withdrawal.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is reviewing the care plan of a patient with schizophrenia. Which finding BEST demonstrates that the nursing intervention aimed at improving medication adherence has been successful?

choices.text: The patient can explain the prescribed medication regimen and its important adverse effects
The patient refuses to discuss medication
The patient's family administers all medication without involving the patient
The patient reports stopping medication because symptoms have improved

questions.rationale: The ability to explain the medication regimen and important adverse effects demonstrates improved treatment knowledge and informed participation. Actual adherence should also be assessed rather than assuming that knowledge alone guarantees medication use.

distractor_rationales.B: Refusal to discuss medication does not demonstrate improved treatment understanding.
distractor_rationales.C: Excluding the patient from medication education does not establish individual understanding or participation.
distractor_rationales.D: Stopping medication without clinical advice indicates a potential adherence problem.

questions.question_text: A patient with a history of suicide attempts becomes unusually cheerful after several days of severe depression and tells the nurse that everything is finally settled. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Assume that the patient has completely recovered
Discontinue suicide precautions immediately
Encourage immediate discharge
Reassess suicide risk, including current thoughts, plans, intentions and access to means

questions.rationale: A sudden change in mood does not necessarily indicate recovery, particularly in a patient with a history of suicide attempts. Comprehensive reassessment is necessary because suicide risk may persist or increase despite apparent improvement in mood.

distractor_rationales.A: Sudden cheerfulness alone is insufficient evidence of complete recovery.
distractor_rationales.B: Safety precautions should only be modified following an appropriate clinical risk assessment.
distractor_rationales.C: Discharge without reassessment may expose the patient to serious harm.

questions.question_text: A patient with severe anxiety is unable to participate in group activities and reports difficulty sleeping. Which intervention should the nurse include in the care plan?

choices.text: Force the patient to participate in every group activity
Establish a supportive relationship and introduce appropriate relaxation and sleep-promoting strategies
Avoid all communication with the patient
Encourage the patient to consume alcohol before sleeping

questions.rationale: A supportive therapeutic relationship provides psychological safety and encourages the patient to express anxiety. Relaxation techniques, structured activities and appropriate sleep hygiene can improve coping and sleep without unnecessarily overwhelming the patient.

distractor_rationales.A: Forcing participation may increase anxiety and resistance to treatment.
distractor_rationales.C: Avoiding communication prevents the development of a therapeutic relationship.
distractor_rationales.D: Alcohol can worsen sleep quality and create additional health and dependence problems.

questions.question_text: A nurse in a psychiatric facility in Ghana receives information that a patient believes traditional spiritual forces are responsible for their illness. Which approach demonstrates culturally sensitive critical thinking?

choices.text: Ridicule the patient's traditional beliefs
Automatically conclude that spiritual beliefs prove the patient has psychosis
Explore the patient's cultural understanding while assessing symptoms and applying evidence-based care
Discontinue psychiatric treatment and recommend only traditional healing

questions.rationale: Culturally sensitive psychiatric assessment requires understanding the patient's explanatory model of illness without automatically interpreting culturally shared beliefs as psychopathology. The nurse should assess functional impairment, associated symptoms and safety while providing respectful, evidence-based care.

distractor_rationales.A: Ridiculing cultural beliefs damages trust and the therapeutic relationship.
distractor_rationales.B: Culturally accepted spiritual beliefs alone are insufficient to establish a psychiatric diagnosis.
distractor_rationales.D: Replacing evidence-based psychiatric treatment with unassessed traditional remedies may compromise patient safety.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of routine antenatal care?

choices.text: To identify and manage maternal and fetal complications while promoting a healthy pregnancy
To guarantee that every pregnancy will end without complications
To determine only the sex of the fetus
To provide treatment only when labour begins

questions.rationale: Antenatal care promotes maternal and fetal health through screening, prevention, health education and early identification of complications. In Ghana, routine antenatal services also provide opportunities to screen for hypertension, anaemia, infections and psychosocial concerns.

distractor_rationales.B: Antenatal care reduces risks but cannot guarantee a complication-free pregnancy.
distractor_rationales.C: Determining fetal sex is not the primary purpose of antenatal care.
distractor_rationales.D: Antenatal care begins during pregnancy and continues before the onset of labour.

questions.question_text: The first stage of labour is defined as the period between:

choices.text: Delivery of the baby and delivery of the placenta
The onset of established labour and full cervical dilatation
Full cervical dilatation and delivery of the baby
Delivery of the placenta and the first 24 hours postpartum

questions.rationale: The first stage of labour extends from the onset of established labour until full cervical dilatation, usually 10 cm. It involves progressive cervical effacement and dilatation under the influence of uterine contractions.

distractor_rationales.A: This describes the interval between the second and third stages of labour.
distractor_rationales.C: This describes the second stage of labour.
distractor_rationales.D: This describes the period following placental delivery rather than the first stage of labour.

questions.question_text: A woman develops heavy vaginal bleeding immediately after delivery. Her uterus feels soft and poorly contracted. What is the MOST likely cause?

choices.text: Uterine atony
Cervical ectropion
Normal uterine involution
Physiological lactation

questions.rationale: Uterine atony occurs when the uterus fails to contract effectively following childbirth, allowing continued bleeding from the placental implantation site. It is a leading cause of postpartum haemorrhage and requires immediate management using the facility's postpartum haemorrhage protocol.

distractor_rationales.B: Cervical ectropion does not explain a poorly contracted uterus with immediate postpartum heavy bleeding.
distractor_rationales.C: Normal uterine involution involves uterine contraction and does not cause uncontrolled haemorrhage.
distractor_rationales.D: Lactation is not the cause of severe immediate postpartum bleeding.

questions.question_text: Which clinical feature distinguishes eclampsia from pre-eclampsia?

choices.text: Mild ankle oedema
Proteinuria alone
New-onset generalised seizures associated with pre-eclampsia, not explained by another cause
Nausea during early pregnancy

questions.rationale: Eclampsia is characterised by new-onset seizures in a woman with pre-eclampsia, when another cause does not explain the convulsions. It is an obstetric emergency requiring maternal stabilisation, seizure management and appropriate delivery planning.

distractor_rationales.A: Oedema may occur during pregnancy and does not independently distinguish eclampsia.
distractor_rationales.B: Proteinuria may occur in pre-eclampsia but does not establish eclampsia.
distractor_rationales.D: Nausea is a nonspecific symptom and does not distinguish eclampsia.

questions.question_text: A woman develops severe confusion, bizarre beliefs and auditory hallucinations five days after giving birth. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Normal postpartum adjustment
Postpartum psychosis
Ordinary pregnancy-related fatigue
Mild postpartum blues

questions.rationale: Postpartum psychosis is a severe psychiatric emergency characterised by symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, confusion and disorganised behaviour, commonly developing in the early postpartum period. Immediate psychiatric and obstetric assessment is necessary because the mother and infant may be at risk of serious harm.

distractor_rationales.A: Confusion, hallucinations and bizarre beliefs are not normal postpartum adjustment symptoms.
distractor_rationales.C: Ordinary fatigue does not explain psychotic symptoms.
distractor_rationales.D: Postpartum blues typically involve transient emotional changes without frank psychosis.

questions.question_text: Which investigation is particularly important during antenatal care for identifying anaemia in a pregnant woman?

choices.text: Haemoglobin estimation
Visual acuity testing alone
Electrocardiography alone
Hearing assessment

questions.rationale: Haemoglobin estimation helps identify anaemia, a significant maternal health concern in Ghana. Early detection allows appropriate investigation and management, including iron and folic acid supplementation and treatment of underlying causes.

distractor_rationales.B: Visual acuity testing does not directly determine haemoglobin concentration.
distractor_rationales.C: Electrocardiography assesses cardiac electrical activity rather than diagnosing anaemia.
distractor_rationales.D: Hearing assessment is not a routine diagnostic investigation for maternal anaemia.

questions.question_text: A woman in active labour is admitted to a maternity unit. The nurse observes regular uterine contractions and progressive cervical dilatation. Which assessment is particularly important for monitoring fetal wellbeing?

choices.text: Maternal hair condition
Maternal food preferences
Fetal heart rate according to the applicable intrapartum monitoring protocol
Maternal educational qualification

questions.rationale: Fetal heart rate monitoring helps identify possible fetal compromise during labour. Intrapartum assessment should follow the appropriate clinical protocol and consider contraction frequency, maternal condition and other findings.

distractor_rationales.A: Hair condition does not provide information about fetal oxygenation or wellbeing.
distractor_rationales.B: Food preferences do not assess fetal wellbeing.
distractor_rationales.D: Educational qualification is relevant to health communication but not direct fetal monitoring.

questions.question_text: A woman develops postpartum haemorrhage following vaginal delivery. The uterus is boggy on palpation. Which intervention should the nurse initiate as part of immediate first-line management?

choices.text: Encourage the woman to walk around
Perform uterine massage while activating the postpartum haemorrhage response
Give oral fluids and wait for the bleeding to stop
Apply a warm compress to the forehead

questions.rationale: A boggy uterus suggests uterine atony, and uterine massage helps stimulate uterine contraction as part of immediate management. The nurse must simultaneously call for help, assess blood loss and circulation, establish appropriate intravenous access and support administration of prescribed uterotonics and other indicated interventions.

distractor_rationales.A: Walking during active postpartum haemorrhage increases risk and delays emergency management.
distractor_rationales.C: Oral fluids are insufficient for managing significant acute blood loss.
distractor_rationales.D: A forehead compress does not address uterine atony or haemorrhage.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks presents with blood pressure of 170/115 mmHg, severe headache and visual disturbances. Which condition is MOST likely?

choices.text: Normal physiological changes of pregnancy
Gestational diabetes
Severe pre-eclampsia
Uncomplicated urinary tract infection

questions.rationale: Severe-range hypertension accompanied by neurological symptoms is strongly suggestive of severe pre-eclampsia. The woman requires urgent obstetric assessment, maternal stabilisation, seizure prophylaxis when indicated and appropriate planning for delivery.

distractor_rationales.A: Severe hypertension and visual disturbances are not normal physiological changes of pregnancy.
distractor_rationales.B: Gestational diabetes is characterised by glucose intolerance and does not explain these findings.
distractor_rationales.D: A urinary tract infection does not adequately explain severe hypertension with neurological symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which statement BEST distinguishes postpartum depression from postpartum blues?

choices.text: Postpartum depression involves more persistent and clinically significant depressive symptoms that impair functioning
Postpartum blues always involve hallucinations and delusions
Postpartum depression occurs only during pregnancy
Postpartum blues always require compulsory psychiatric admission

questions.rationale: Postpartum depression involves persistent depressive symptoms, such as low mood, loss of interest, hopelessness and impaired functioning. Postpartum blues are generally milder and transient, whereas depression requires clinical assessment and appropriate treatment.

distractor_rationales.B: Hallucinations and delusions suggest postpartum psychosis rather than ordinary postpartum blues.
distractor_rationales.C: Postpartum depression develops after childbirth, although depressive episodes can also begin during pregnancy.
distractor_rationales.D: Postpartum blues do not routinely require psychiatric admission.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman experiencing an eclamptic seizure is brought to the emergency maternity unit. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?

choices.text: Insert a spoon into the patient's mouth
Attempt to restrain all limb movements forcefully
Protect the patient from injury, position laterally when feasible and maintain airway and breathing
Administer oral antihypertensive medication during the seizure

questions.rationale: During an eclamptic seizure, immediate maternal priorities are injury prevention, airway protection and adequate oxygenation. The nurse should summon emergency assistance and prepare for prescribed magnesium sulphate treatment and subsequent obstetric management.

distractor_rationales.A: Inserting objects into the mouth may cause dental injury and airway obstruction.
distractor_rationales.B: Forceful restraint may cause musculoskeletal injuries and does not stop the seizure.
distractor_rationales.D: Oral medication is unsafe during an active seizure because of aspiration risk.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour suddenly develops severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding and signs of maternal shock. What serious obstetric complication should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Placental abruption
Normal cervical dilatation
Physiological Braxton Hicks contractions
Normal fetal movement

questions.rationale: Placental abruption involves premature separation of the normally implanted placenta and may cause painful vaginal bleeding, uterine tenderness and maternal haemodynamic instability. It requires urgent obstetric intervention and continuous assessment of maternal and fetal wellbeing.

distractor_rationales.B: Normal cervical dilatation does not explain maternal shock and severe abdominal pain.
distractor_rationales.C: Braxton Hicks contractions are generally irregular and do not cause haemorrhagic shock.
distractor_rationales.D: Normal fetal movement does not explain the maternal signs of acute blood loss.

questions.question_text: A nurse is attending to four postpartum women. Which patient should be assessed FIRST?

choices.text: A woman with mild perineal discomfort after an uncomplicated delivery
A woman breastfeeding comfortably with stable vital signs
A woman with a boggy uterus, heavy vaginal bleeding and increasing pulse rate
A woman requesting assistance with newborn bathing

questions.rationale: A boggy uterus, heavy bleeding and tachycardia suggest postpartum haemorrhage with possible developing hypovolaemic shock. Immediate emergency assessment and management are required to prevent maternal death.

distractor_rationales.A: Mild perineal discomfort requires care but is not immediately life-threatening.
distractor_rationales.B: A woman with stable vital signs and comfortable breastfeeding does not present an immediate emergency.
distractor_rationales.D: Newborn bathing assistance is routine care and can be delayed.

questions.question_text: A woman with a history of bipolar disorder gives birth and subsequently develops severe insomnia, grandiose beliefs and disorganised behaviour. Which nursing action is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Reassure her that these behaviours are normal after childbirth
Arrange urgent psychiatric assessment and ensure the safety of both mother and infant
Leave her alone with the newborn to promote bonding
Discharge her because postpartum mood changes are expected

questions.rationale: The symptoms suggest possible postpartum psychosis, and a history of bipolar disorder increases the risk. Immediate specialist assessment, appropriate observation and a safety plan for mother and infant are essential.

distractor_rationales.A: Grandiose delusions and disorganised behaviour are not normal postpartum adjustments.
distractor_rationales.C: Leaving a potentially psychotic mother unsupervised with the infant may expose both to harm.
distractor_rationales.D: Discharging the patient without urgent assessment would be unsafe.

questions.question_text: A nurse in a Ghanaian maternity unit is caring for four women. Which patient requires immediate attention?

choices.text: A woman at 38 weeks with mild irregular contractions
A woman with severe pre-eclampsia who develops sudden convulsions
A woman requesting information about breastfeeding
A woman with mild nausea during the first stage of labour

questions.rationale: Convulsions in a woman with severe pre-eclampsia indicate eclampsia, a life-threatening obstetric emergency. Immediate airway protection, emergency assistance, seizure management and maternal stabilisation take priority.

distractor_rationales.A: Mild irregular contractions require assessment but do not represent the same immediate danger.
distractor_rationales.C: Breastfeeding education is important but can wait.
distractor_rationales.D: Mild nausea during labour is less urgent than an active eclamptic seizure.

topics: Child Mental Health and Behavioural Disorders

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes growth from development?

choices.text: Growth refers to quantitative physical changes, while development refers to progressive acquisition of functional abilities
Growth refers only to emotional changes, while development refers only to body weight
Growth and development have exactly the same meaning
Development stops completely after infancy

questions.rationale: Growth involves measurable increases in physical dimensions, such as height, weight and head circumference. Development refers to progressive changes in motor, cognitive, language, social and emotional functioning.

distractor_rationales.B: The definitions of growth and development are incorrectly reversed and restricted.
distractor_rationales.C: Growth and development are related but distinct processes.
distractor_rationales.D: Development continues throughout childhood and into adulthood.

questions.question_text: A mother brings her 18-month-old child to a child welfare clinic in Ghana. Which developmental ability would generally be expected at this age?

choices.text: Walking independently and attempting simple words
Writing complete sentences
Solving complex mathematical problems
Reading paragraphs independently

questions.rationale: By approximately 18 months, many children can walk independently and use several meaningful words, although individual developmental variation occurs. Developmental surveillance should assess gross motor, fine motor, language, cognitive and social milestones.

distractor_rationales.B: Writing complete sentences is an advanced skill that is not expected at 18 months.
distractor_rationales.C: Complex mathematical reasoning is not an expected toddler developmental ability.
distractor_rationales.D: Independent paragraph reading is not an expected milestone at this age.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of childhood immunisation?

choices.text: To expose children to dangerous infections
To stimulate protective immune responses against specific infectious diseases
To eliminate the need for all future medical care
To treat established bacterial infections immediately

questions.rationale: Immunisation stimulates the immune system to develop protection against specific infectious diseases. Ghana's Expanded Programme on Immunisation helps prevent childhood morbidity and mortality from vaccine-preventable diseases.

distractor_rationales.A: Vaccines are designed to stimulate immunity safely rather than deliberately expose children to dangerous infections.
distractor_rationales.C: Immunisation does not eliminate the need for other preventive and curative healthcare.
distractor_rationales.D: Vaccines primarily prevent disease and are not substitutes for treatment of established infections.

questions.question_text: A 2-year-old child presents to a clinic with diarrhoea, sunken eyes, dry mouth and reduced urine output. The child is alert and able to drink. Which intervention is MOST appropriate for managing dehydration when severe dehydration is absent?

choices.text: Withhold all oral fluids
Administer antidiarrhoeal drugs without assessment
Give appropriate oral rehydration solution and continue feeding and breastfeeding
Restrict breastfeeding until diarrhoea stops

questions.rationale: Oral rehydration solution replaces water and electrolytes lost through diarrhoea and is appropriate for children who can drink and do not have severe dehydration. Continued breastfeeding, appropriate feeding and zinc supplementation according to national guidelines support recovery.

distractor_rationales.A: Withholding fluids worsens dehydration.
distractor_rationales.B: Routine antidiarrhoeal drugs are generally not recommended for young children and may cause harm.
distractor_rationales.D: Breastfeeding should continue during diarrhoeal illness.

questions.question_text: Which intervention is most effective in preventing hypothermia in a healthy newborn immediately after birth?

choices.text: Bathing the newborn immediately
Placing the newborn near an open window
Leaving the newborn uncovered for routine observation
Drying the newborn thoroughly and initiating skin-to-skin contact with the mother

questions.rationale: Immediate drying removes evaporative heat loss, while skin-to-skin contact helps maintain the newborn's temperature. Delayed bathing, appropriate clothing and early breastfeeding are additional essential components of newborn thermal care.

distractor_rationales.A: Immediate bathing increases heat loss and should be delayed.
distractor_rationales.B: An open window may expose the newborn to cold air and increase heat loss.
distractor_rationales.C: Leaving a newborn uncovered increases the risk of hypothermia.

questions.question_text: A 3-year-old child attending a child welfare clinic speaks very few words, rarely makes eye contact and does not respond consistently when called by name. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Assume the child is deliberately refusing to communicate
Recommend immediate punishment for poor communication
Conduct developmental screening and arrange further assessment for possible developmental disorders
Tell the parents that all children develop at exactly the same rate

questions.rationale: Limited language, reduced social interaction and inconsistent response to name may indicate developmental delay or autism spectrum disorder. The nurse should assess developmental history, conduct appropriate screening and facilitate referral for comprehensive evaluation and early intervention.

distractor_rationales.A: The behaviours may reflect developmental difficulties rather than deliberate refusal.
distractor_rationales.B: Punishment does not address possible underlying developmental conditions.
distractor_rationales.D: Developmental milestones vary, and significant concerns require assessment rather than dismissal.

questions.question_text: A mother brings her infant for routine immunisation but reports that the child has a mild common cold without fever and is feeding normally. What should the nurse generally do?

choices.text: Automatically postpone every vaccine for one month
Assess the child and proceed with indicated immunisation if there is no valid contraindication
Give double doses of all vaccines
Permanently discontinue the child's immunisation schedule

questions.rationale: A mild respiratory illness without significant systemic symptoms is generally not a contraindication to routine vaccination. The nurse should assess the child and follow Ghana's current immunisation schedule and vaccine-specific contraindications.

distractor_rationales.A: Mild illness alone does not normally justify postponing routine immunisation.
distractor_rationales.C: Vaccine doses must follow the recommended schedule and should never be doubled to compensate for mild illness.
distractor_rationales.D: A mild cold is not a reason to discontinue childhood immunisation.

questions.question_text: A child with acute diarrhoea becomes lethargic, is unable to drink and has very sunken eyes. Which classification is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: No dehydration
Mild dehydration only
Severe dehydration
Fluid overload

questions.rationale: Lethargy, inability to drink and very sunken eyes are danger signs consistent with severe dehydration under the WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness approach. The child requires urgent facility-based rehydration and close monitoring, with intravenous treatment when indicated by the applicable protocol.

distractor_rationales.A: The child demonstrates multiple serious signs of fluid depletion.
distractor_rationales.B: The presence of lethargy and inability to drink indicates a more severe condition.
distractor_rationales.D: Fluid overload produces fluid accumulation rather than the described signs of dehydration.

questions.question_text: A newborn develops yellow discolouration of the skin within the first 18 hours after birth. What is the MOST appropriate nursing action?

choices.text: Reassure the mother that early jaundice is always normal
Initiate urgent clinical assessment and arrange bilirubin evaluation
Stop breastfeeding permanently
Discharge the newborn without further examination

questions.rationale: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is pathological until proven otherwise and requires urgent assessment. Bilirubin measurement and investigation of the underlying cause are necessary because severe neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia can lead to bilirubin encephalopathy.

distractor_rationales.A: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is not considered routine physiological jaundice.
distractor_rationales.C: Breastfeeding should not be permanently discontinued without a specific clinical indication.
distractor_rationales.D: Discharging the newborn without assessment risks missing potentially serious neonatal disease.

questions.topic: Child Mental Health and Behavioural Disorders
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)?

choices.text: Persistent inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that causes functional impairment
Temporary sadness after losing a toy
A single episode of fever and vomiting
Normal age-appropriate curiosity without functional impairment

questions.rationale: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by persistent patterns of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interfere with functioning. Symptoms should be developmentally inappropriate, occur across more than one setting and have an appropriate history before diagnosis.

distractor_rationales.B: Temporary sadness is a normal emotional response and does not establish ADHD.
distractor_rationales.C: Fever and vomiting are physical symptoms unrelated to the diagnostic features of ADHD.
distractor_rationales.D: Normal curiosity without functional impairment is not sufficient to diagnose ADHD.

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old child presents to a district hospital with fever, cough, fast breathing and chest indrawing. What should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Uncomplicated constipation
Pneumonia with possible severe respiratory involvement
Normal respiratory adaptation
Simple skin allergy

questions.rationale: Fever, cough, fast breathing and chest indrawing are important clinical indicators of pneumonia in a child. Chest indrawing suggests significant respiratory involvement and requires prompt assessment, appropriate treatment and monitoring for hypoxaemia.

distractor_rationales.A: Constipation does not explain the respiratory symptoms.
distractor_rationales.C: Chest indrawing and fast breathing are abnormal findings requiring clinical assessment.
distractor_rationales.D: A skin allergy does not explain the child's respiratory presentation.

questions.topic: Child Mental Health and Behavioural Disorders
questions.question_text: A mother reports that her 9-year-old child frequently has difficulty maintaining attention, interrupts conversations and struggles to remain seated both at home and school. What is the MOST appropriate nursing action?

choices.text: Immediately label the child as disobedient
Recommend physical punishment
Obtain developmental and behavioural history and facilitate appropriate assessment for ADHD
Advise the mother to withdraw the child from school

questions.rationale: Persistent inattention and hyperactivity across home and school settings may indicate ADHD. Assessment should establish symptom duration, developmental appropriateness, functional impairment and possible alternative explanations before diagnosis.

distractor_rationales.A: Labelling the child as disobedient ignores the possibility of an underlying neurodevelopmental disorder.
distractor_rationales.B: Physical punishment is not an evidence-based treatment for ADHD.
distractor_rationales.D: School withdrawal may worsen educational and social outcomes rather than address the underlying difficulties.

questions.question_text: A nurse is caring for four children in a paediatric ward. Which child should be assessed FIRST?

choices.text: A child with uncomplicated malaria who is alert and drinking
A child with mild eczema and itching
A child with diarrhoea who is playful and feeding normally
A child with severe pneumonia who has central cyanosis and marked respiratory distress

questions.rationale: Central cyanosis and severe respiratory distress indicate potentially life-threatening hypoxaemia. The nurse must prioritise airway and breathing assessment, emergency oxygenation support according to protocol and urgent escalation.

distractor_rationales.A: An alert child with uncomplicated malaria requires treatment but does not have the same immediate respiratory threat.
distractor_rationales.B: Mild eczema is not an immediate life-threatening condition.
distractor_rationales.C: A playful child who is feeding normally is less urgent than a child with severe respiratory compromise.

questions.question_text: A newborn is delivered in a Ghanaian health facility and is not breathing adequately after initial drying and stimulation. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Wait for five minutes to see whether spontaneous breathing develops
Initiate appropriate neonatal resuscitation, including effective positive-pressure ventilation when indicated
Give oral glucose immediately
Place the newborn in a cold bath

questions.rationale: A newborn who remains apnoeic or gasping after initial steps requires prompt neonatal resuscitation, with effective positive-pressure ventilation as the critical intervention. Delaying ventilation increases the risk of hypoxic injury and neonatal death.

distractor_rationales.A: Waiting unnecessarily delays life-saving ventilation.
distractor_rationales.C: Oral glucose does not correct neonatal respiratory failure and may cause aspiration.
distractor_rationales.D: Cold bathing causes heat loss and is dangerous for a compromised newborn.

questions.question_text: A nurse is attending to four children in a Ghanaian paediatric emergency unit. Which child requires immediate attention?

choices.text: A child with mild diarrhoea who is drinking normally
A child with a mild cough and normal respiratory rate
A child with severe dehydration who is lethargic, unable to drink and has signs of circulatory compromise
A child with mild skin itching

questions.rationale: Lethargy, inability to drink and circulatory compromise indicate severe dehydration with a risk of hypovolaemic shock. The child requires immediate emergency assessment, appropriate intravenous rehydration when indicated and continuous monitoring.

distractor_rationales.A: Mild diarrhoea without danger signs can generally be managed using appropriate oral rehydration and monitoring.
distractor_rationales.B: A child with normal respiratory function and a mild cough is not the immediate priority.
distractor_rationales.D: Mild itching is not an immediate life-threatening emergency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes therapeutic communication in psychiatric nursing?

choices.text: Purposeful communication that promotes understanding, trust and positive patient outcomes
Communication intended to impose the nurse's personal beliefs
Casual conversation that avoids the patient's emotional concerns
Communication that prevents patients from expressing their feelings

questions.rationale: Therapeutic communication is a purposeful professional interaction used to establish trust, facilitate emotional expression and support recovery. It is central to psychiatric nursing because patients may experience fear, stigma, altered perception and difficulties expressing their needs.

distractor_rationales.B: Imposing personal beliefs violates professional boundaries and patient autonomy.
distractor_rationales.C: Avoiding emotional concerns prevents meaningful therapeutic engagement.
distractor_rationales.D: Patients should be encouraged to express their feelings in a safe and supportive environment.

questions.question_text: A patient with depression tells the nurse, 'Nobody cares about me, and I feel completely alone.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?

choices.text: You should stop thinking that way
Many people have worse problems than you
Can you tell me more about what makes you feel alone?
You are wrong because your family visits you

questions.rationale: An open-ended response encourages the patient to explore and express emotional experiences. It demonstrates empathy and provides an opportunity to identify contributing factors, including possible depressive symptoms and suicide risk.

distractor_rationales.A: This response dismisses the patient's feelings.
distractor_rationales.B: Comparing suffering minimises the patient's emotional experience.
distractor_rationales.D: Arguing with the patient may discourage further communication.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of involving family members in psychiatric care when the patient consents and involvement is appropriate?

choices.text: To transfer all treatment responsibilities from healthcare professionals to relatives
To strengthen support, improve understanding and promote continuity of care
To allow relatives to make every decision regardless of the patient's capacity
To prevent the patient from participating in treatment decisions

questions.rationale: Family involvement can improve treatment understanding, medication support, relapse prevention and community reintegration. In Ghana, supportive family participation is particularly valuable in community psychiatric care, provided confidentiality, patient rights and consent are respected.

distractor_rationales.A: Healthcare professionals retain their clinical responsibilities even when families participate in care.
distractor_rationales.C: Family involvement does not automatically remove a patient's decision-making rights.
distractor_rationales.D: Family-centred care promotes patient participation rather than excluding the patient.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia is being denied information about a proposed treatment because the healthcare team assumes the patient cannot understand. What should the psychiatric nurse do?

choices.text: Support the patient's right to receive understandable information and participate in decisions
Agree that psychiatric patients should never receive treatment information
Allow relatives to make every decision without assessing the patient's capacity
Avoid discussing the treatment to prevent disagreement

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy requires protecting the patient's rights, dignity and access to appropriate information. A psychiatric diagnosis alone does not establish incapacity; decision-making capacity must be assessed in relation to the particular decision.

distractor_rationales.B: Psychiatric patients retain the right to receive appropriate treatment information.
distractor_rationales.C: Family members do not automatically replace the patient's decision-making authority.
distractor_rationales.D: Avoiding discussion prevents informed participation and violates patient-centred care.

questions.question_text: A patient from a Ghanaian community believes that mental illness may be caused by spiritual influences. What is the MOST appropriate response by the psychiatric nurse?

choices.text: Mock the patient's beliefs and insist that they are irrational
Immediately discharge the patient to seek traditional treatment
Explore the patient's beliefs respectfully while providing evidence-based psychiatric care
Assume that the patient has a delusional disorder solely because of the belief

questions.rationale: Culturally sensitive care recognises that individuals may have different explanations for mental illness. The nurse should explore the patient's beliefs respectfully while assessing whether they are culturally shared or represent psychopathological symptoms and ensuring appropriate clinical treatment.

distractor_rationales.A: Mocking cultural beliefs damages trust and discourages treatment engagement.
distractor_rationales.B: Discharging a patient without appropriate clinical assessment may expose the patient to harm.
distractor_rationales.D: A culturally shared spiritual belief alone is insufficient to establish a psychiatric diagnosis.

questions.question_text: Which statement BEST represents mental health stigma?

choices.text: The negative attitudes, stereotypes and discriminatory behaviours directed towards people with mental health conditions
The provision of equal healthcare services to all patients
The protection of patient confidentiality
The process of promoting community reintegration

questions.rationale: Mental health stigma involves negative stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination against people with mental health conditions. It can discourage treatment seeking, reduce social participation and worsen health inequalities in Ghanaian communities.

distractor_rationales.B: Equal healthcare provision is an example of reducing discrimination rather than stigma.
distractor_rationales.C: Confidentiality protects patient rights and is not an example of stigma.
distractor_rationales.D: Community reintegration promotes inclusion and helps reduce stigma.

questions.question_text: A patient experiencing auditory hallucinations tells the nurse, 'The voices are telling me that I am evil.' Which response is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Yes, the voices are telling you the truth
I do not hear the voices, but I can see that they are frightening you
Stop imagining things because they are not real
You should listen carefully to everything the voices say

questions.rationale: The nurse should acknowledge the patient's emotional experience without confirming the hallucination. This response maintains reality orientation while demonstrating empathy and encouraging further discussion about the patient's distress and safety.

distractor_rationales.A: Agreeing with the hallucination reinforces the patient's altered perception.
distractor_rationales.C: Dismissing the experience may damage the therapeutic relationship.
distractor_rationales.D: Encouraging obedience to hallucinations may expose the patient to harm.

questions.question_text: A family in a rural Ghanaian community refuses to bring their relative with schizophrenia to a psychiatric facility because they believe the illness is caused by spiritual forces. What should the community psychiatric nurse do?

choices.text: Threaten the family with legal action immediately
Ignore the patient because the family has refused treatment
Explore the family's concerns, provide mental health education and facilitate appropriate referral
Encourage the family to use unverified remedies instead of professional care

questions.rationale: Respectful engagement and culturally appropriate mental health education can reduce misconceptions and encourage treatment seeking. The nurse should facilitate access to psychiatric services through available community structures, including CHPS and community mental health services.

distractor_rationales.A: Threatening the family may increase resistance and undermine community engagement.
distractor_rationales.B: Ignoring the patient neglects the nurse's professional responsibility to facilitate access to care.
distractor_rationales.D: Unverified remedies should not replace appropriate psychiatric assessment and treatment.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving psychiatric treatment informs the nurse that another healthcare worker has disclosed the patient's diagnosis to unrelated community members. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the complaint because mental illness is a public issue
Discuss the patient's diagnosis publicly to correct the information
Tell the patient that confidentiality does not apply in psychiatric care
Listen to the complaint, protect confidentiality and report the suspected breach through appropriate channels

questions.rationale: Confidentiality is a fundamental professional and ethical obligation in psychiatric nursing. The nurse should respond appropriately to the complaint, safeguard the patient's information and follow facility procedures for reporting and addressing confidentiality breaches.

distractor_rationales.A: Mental illness does not remove the patient's right to confidentiality.
distractor_rationales.B: Further public disclosure would worsen the original breach.
distractor_rationales.C: Confidentiality applies to psychiatric patients, subject to lawful and justified exceptions.

questions.question_text: A patient becomes silent and begins crying during a discussion about the death of a parent. Which nursing response is MOST therapeutic?

choices.text: Remain present and allow the patient time to express emotions
Immediately change the subject
Tell the patient that crying is a sign of weakness
Leave without explaining why

questions.rationale: Therapeutic silence allows the patient time to process emotions and communicate when ready. Remaining present demonstrates acceptance, empathy and emotional support.

distractor_rationales.B: Changing the subject may communicate discomfort with the patient's feelings.
distractor_rationales.C: Crying is a normal emotional response and should not be stigmatised.
distractor_rationales.D: Leaving without explanation may make the patient feel abandoned.

questions.question_text: Which community intervention is MOST effective in reducing stigma associated with mental illness in Ghana?

choices.text: Keeping people with mental illness permanently isolated
Conducting community mental health education and promoting social inclusion
Discouraging families from seeking psychiatric services
Using insulting labels to describe psychiatric patients

questions.rationale: Community education and social inclusion help correct misconceptions, reduce discrimination and encourage early treatment seeking. Collaboration with community leaders, families, CHPS compounds and mental health professionals can strengthen these interventions.

distractor_rationales.A: Permanent isolation reinforces discrimination and violates principles of community integration.
distractor_rationales.C: Discouraging treatment seeking can delay appropriate care and worsen outcomes.
distractor_rationales.D: Insulting labels increase stigma and undermine patient dignity.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric patient is preparing for discharge after improvement in symptoms of schizophrenia. Which intervention BEST supports continuity of care?

choices.text: Discharge the patient without discussing follow-up arrangements
Tell the family to manage all psychiatric treatment independently
Develop a discharge plan involving the patient, consenting family members and appropriate community mental health services
Advise the patient to discontinue medication after returning home

questions.rationale: A collaborative discharge plan supports medication continuity, follow-up appointments, relapse prevention and community reintegration. In Ghana, appropriate coordination with community psychiatric nurses and available primary healthcare services can improve continuity of care.

distractor_rationales.A: Discharge without follow-up planning increases the risk of interrupted treatment and relapse.
distractor_rationales.B: Families provide support but should not independently replace professional psychiatric care.
distractor_rationales.D: Stopping prescribed medication without clinical review may increase the risk of relapse.

questions.question_text: A patient with depression refuses a proposed treatment after receiving adequate information and demonstrating decision-making capacity. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force treatment because the patient has a psychiatric diagnosis
Respect the informed refusal, explore the patient's concerns and communicate with the treating team
Threaten to withhold all future nursing care
Ask another patient to persuade the individual through intimidation

questions.rationale: A patient with decision-making capacity has the right to make informed decisions, including refusing proposed treatment, subject to applicable legal provisions and emergency exceptions. The nurse should document the discussion, explore concerns and communicate with the treating team.

distractor_rationales.A: A psychiatric diagnosis alone does not remove a patient's right to make treatment decisions.
distractor_rationales.C: Withholding nursing care as punishment is unethical and violates professional responsibilities.
distractor_rationales.D: Intimidation is not an appropriate approach to informed treatment refusal.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is caring for four patients. Which patient requires the nurse's FIRST attention?

choices.text: A patient requesting assistance with writing a letter
A patient who is quietly participating in an occupational therapy activity
A patient expressing sadness about missing family members
A patient who suddenly becomes aggressive, threatens others and begins picking up objects to throw

questions.rationale: The patient demonstrates escalating aggression and an immediate potential threat to other people. The nurse should prioritise safety, summon assistance and initiate appropriate de-escalation measures.

distractor_rationales.A: Assistance with letter writing is a routine request and can wait.
distractor_rationales.B: The patient is participating appropriately in therapeutic activity.
distractor_rationales.C: Sadness requires therapeutic support but does not indicate immediate danger in this scenario.

questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a patient's family has taken the patient to a traditional healer before seeking psychiatric treatment. Which action is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Condemn the family and refuse further communication
Assume that the patient has no psychiatric condition
Respectfully explore the family's experiences and encourage safe, evidence-based treatment
Advise the family to abandon all hospital treatment permanently

questions.rationale: Respectful engagement helps establish trust and provides an opportunity to address misconceptions about mental illness. The nurse should promote safe treatment, discourage harmful practices and facilitate appropriate psychiatric care without unnecessary cultural judgement.

distractor_rationales.A: Condemning the family may discourage future engagement with mental health services.
distractor_rationales.B: Consultation with a traditional healer does not establish whether a psychiatric condition is present or absent.
distractor_rationales.D: Abandoning hospital treatment may delay necessary clinical interventions.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is attending to four patients. Which situation requires immediate intervention?

choices.text: A family asking for information about schizophrenia
A patient expressing an intention to kill a family member and identifying a specific plan
A patient requesting a visit from a relative
A patient asking about community rehabilitation services

questions.rationale: A specific threat and plan to kill another person indicate a potentially imminent risk of serious violence. The nurse must immediately implement appropriate safety measures, notify the treating team and follow relevant legal and institutional procedures.

distractor_rationales.A: Family education is important but is not an immediate emergency.
distractor_rationales.C: A visitation request is a routine patient need.
distractor_rationales.D: Community rehabilitation information can be provided after immediate safety concerns are addressed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common extrapyramidal adverse effect associated with first-generation antipsychotic medications?

choices.text: Acute dystonia
Hyperglycaemia in every patient
Improved muscle coordination
Increased visual acuity

questions.rationale: First-generation antipsychotics, particularly high-potency agents, can cause extrapyramidal symptoms such as acute dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia and tardive dyskinesia. These adverse effects result primarily from dopamine D2 receptor blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway.

distractor_rationales.B: Hyperglycaemia is a possible metabolic adverse effect of some antipsychotics but is not an extrapyramidal symptom.
distractor_rationales.C: Antipsychotic-induced extrapyramidal symptoms impair rather than improve movement.
distractor_rationales.D: Increased visual acuity is not a recognised extrapyramidal adverse effect.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving haloperidol develops sudden painful neck twisting, upward deviation of the eyes and difficulty swallowing. Which adverse effect should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Tardive dyskinesia
Acute dystonia
Hypoglycaemia
Serotonin withdrawal syndrome

questions.rationale: Sudden involuntary muscle contractions involving the neck and eyes are characteristic of acute dystonia associated with antipsychotic treatment. Difficulty swallowing raises concern about possible airway involvement, requiring immediate assessment, withholding further doses pending urgent review and prescribed treatment such as an anticholinergic.

distractor_rationales.A: Tardive dyskinesia usually involves persistent repetitive movements, commonly affecting the face and tongue, after prolonged exposure.
distractor_rationales.C: Hypoglycaemia does not typically cause sustained involuntary neck twisting and oculogyric crisis.
distractor_rationales.D: Serotonin withdrawal syndrome is not the characteristic explanation for acute dystonic reactions.

questions.question_text: Which combination of findings is most consistent with metabolic syndrome?

choices.text: Central obesity, elevated blood pressure, raised blood glucose and dyslipidaemia
Low blood glucose, low blood pressure and reduced waist circumference
Anaemia, fever and dehydration
Bradycardia, low body temperature and weight loss

questions.rationale: Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors that includes central obesity, hypertension, elevated glucose and abnormal lipid levels. Some psychiatric medications, particularly certain second-generation antipsychotics, increase the risk of metabolic abnormalities.

distractor_rationales.B: These findings do not represent the characteristic cluster of metabolic syndrome.
distractor_rationales.C: Anaemia, fever and dehydration are not diagnostic components of metabolic syndrome.
distractor_rationales.D: Bradycardia and weight loss are not the defining metabolic syndrome features.

questions.question_text: A patient taking lithium for bipolar disorder develops coarse tremors, vomiting, diarrhoea, unsteady gait and confusion. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Lithium toxicity
Normal therapeutic response
Iron deficiency anaemia
Uncomplicated allergic rhinitis

questions.rationale: Coarse tremors, gastrointestinal symptoms, ataxia and confusion are concerning manifestations of lithium toxicity. The nurse should withhold further lithium pending urgent medical review, assess hydration and neurological status, and arrange serum lithium and renal function testing.

distractor_rationales.B: Coarse tremors, ataxia and confusion are warning signs of toxicity rather than an acceptable therapeutic response.
distractor_rationales.C: Iron deficiency anaemia does not adequately explain the characteristic neurological and gastrointestinal findings.
distractor_rationales.D: Allergic rhinitis causes nasal symptoms and does not explain lithium-associated neurological deterioration.

questions.question_text: Which physical health assessment is particularly important for a patient receiving long-term second-generation antipsychotic medication?

choices.text: Routine assessment of weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, blood glucose and lipid profile
Assessment of hair length only
Routine hearing assessment only
Assessment of handwriting style only

questions.rationale: Second-generation antipsychotics can contribute to weight gain, dyslipidaemia and hyperglycaemia, increasing cardiovascular risk. Baseline and periodic metabolic monitoring allows early detection and management of these complications.

distractor_rationales.B: Hair length does not assess the metabolic complications associated with antipsychotic medication.
distractor_rationales.C: Hearing assessment alone cannot identify metabolic syndrome.
distractor_rationales.D: Handwriting assessment is not a substitute for routine metabolic monitoring.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving clozapine develops fever, sore throat and general weakness. Which complication should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Agranulocytosis or severe neutropenia
Improved immune function
Simple medication tolerance
Uncomplicated constipation

questions.rationale: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia or agranulocytosis, reducing the patient's ability to fight infections. Fever and sore throat require urgent clinical assessment and a full blood count with absolute neutrophil count according to the monitoring protocol.

distractor_rationales.B: Clozapine-associated neutropenia reduces rather than improves immune defence.
distractor_rationales.C: Fever and sore throat may indicate a serious adverse drug reaction and must not be dismissed as tolerance.
distractor_rationales.D: Constipation is another important clozapine adverse effect but does not explain the infection-related warning signs.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Which nursing intervention is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Concentrate exclusively on psychiatric symptoms
Stop all physical health monitoring because the patient is receiving psychiatric treatment
Integrate physical health monitoring, medication review and lifestyle education into psychiatric care
Assume that diabetes and hypertension are caused entirely by schizophrenia

questions.rationale: People with severe mental illness experience significant physical health inequalities and may have multiple chronic medical conditions. Integrated care should include blood pressure and glucose monitoring, cardiovascular risk assessment, medication review and appropriate health education.

distractor_rationales.A: Psychiatric care must not exclude the assessment and management of physical illnesses.
distractor_rationales.B: Psychiatric treatment does not eliminate the need for physical health monitoring.
distractor_rationales.D: Diabetes and hypertension have multifactorial causes and should not be attributed entirely to schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A patient taking an antipsychotic develops a temperature of 40°C, severe muscle rigidity, confusion and autonomic instability. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Mild anxiety disorder
Uncomplicated insomnia
Seasonal allergic rhinitis

questions.rationale: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a potentially fatal reaction associated with dopamine-blocking medications and is characterised by hyperthermia, severe rigidity, altered mental status and autonomic instability. It requires immediate discontinuation of the suspected causative medication under emergency medical management and urgent supportive treatment.

distractor_rationales.B: Mild anxiety does not explain severe hyperthermia and muscle rigidity.
distractor_rationales.C: Insomnia does not cause the characteristic systemic and neurological features of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
distractor_rationales.D: Allergic rhinitis does not explain severe rigidity and autonomic instability.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric patient taking olanzapine has gained 12 kg over six months. The patient's fasting blood glucose and triglyceride levels have also increased. Which nursing intervention is MOST appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore the changes because weight gain is expected in all psychiatric patients
Encourage dietary and physical activity interventions and arrange clinical review of metabolic risk and medication
Tell the patient to stop olanzapine immediately without medical review
Recommend increasing intake of sugary beverages

questions.rationale: Olanzapine is associated with clinically significant weight gain and metabolic abnormalities. The nurse should promote healthy dietary habits, physical activity and regular metabolic monitoring while discussing possible treatment adjustments with the prescriber.

distractor_rationales.A: Significant weight and metabolic changes require clinical attention rather than being dismissed.
distractor_rationales.C: Abruptly stopping antipsychotic medication without clinical review may cause relapse.
distractor_rationales.D: Sugary beverages can worsen weight gain and hyperglycaemia.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric patient presents with sudden confusion, sweating, tremors and palpitations. The patient has diabetes and uses insulin. What should the nurse do FIRST?

choices.text: Assume that the patient is experiencing a psychiatric relapse
Administer the next scheduled insulin dose
Assess airway and consciousness and immediately check blood glucose
Refer the patient for routine psychotherapy

questions.rationale: The symptoms may indicate hypoglycaemia, which can cause acute behavioural changes and altered consciousness. The nurse must promptly check blood glucose and provide appropriate treatment according to the patient's consciousness and ability to swallow safely.

distractor_rationales.A: Acute confusion and autonomic symptoms require physical health assessment before being attributed to psychiatric relapse.
distractor_rationales.B: Administering insulin during possible hypoglycaemia may worsen the condition.
distractor_rationales.D: Routine psychotherapy does not address a potentially life-threatening metabolic emergency.

questions.question_text: A patient taking an antidepressant develops agitation, sweating, diarrhoea, tremor, hyperreflexia and clonus after another serotonergic medication is introduced. What is the MOST likely condition?

choices.text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Serotonin syndrome
Lithium-induced hypothyroidism
Tardive dyskinesia

questions.rationale: Serotonin syndrome results from excessive serotonergic activity and may cause agitation, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus. It requires urgent recognition, withdrawal of causative serotonergic agents under medical direction and supportive emergency treatment.

distractor_rationales.A: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is more strongly associated with dopamine blockade and typically features severe rigidity and reduced reflexes rather than clonus and hyperreflexia.
distractor_rationales.C: Lithium-induced hypothyroidism does not explain the acute neuromuscular and autonomic findings.
distractor_rationales.D: Tardive dyskinesia generally produces persistent involuntary movements rather than an acute serotonergic toxidrome.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia is admitted with excessive thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision and unexplained weight loss. Which medical condition should the nurse investigate?

choices.text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Acute otitis media
Iron deficiency anaemia alone
Uncomplicated dermatitis

questions.rationale: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision and unexplained weight loss are characteristic symptoms of hyperglycaemia and possible diabetes mellitus. Blood glucose testing and appropriate clinical assessment are required, particularly because some antipsychotic medications increase metabolic risk.

distractor_rationales.B: Otitis media causes ear-related symptoms and does not explain the classical hyperglycaemic presentation.
distractor_rationales.C: Iron deficiency anaemia may cause fatigue and pallor but does not adequately explain polyuria and polydipsia.
distractor_rationales.D: Dermatitis does not cause the characteristic symptoms described.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric patient taking an antipsychotic suddenly develops severe difficulty swallowing, noisy breathing and involuntary neck contractions. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?

choices.text: Encourage the patient to drink water
Document the findings and wait until the next ward round
Arrange routine outpatient follow-up
Activate emergency assistance and assess airway and breathing

questions.rationale: The findings suggest severe acute dystonia with possible laryngeal involvement, which can cause life-threatening airway obstruction. Immediate airway assessment, emergency assistance and prescribed treatment are essential.

distractor_rationales.A: Giving oral fluids to a patient with severe swallowing difficulty increases aspiration risk.
distractor_rationales.B: Waiting for a routine ward round delays treatment of a potential airway emergency.
distractor_rationales.C: Outpatient follow-up is inappropriate for an acute respiratory threat.

questions.question_text: A patient with bipolar disorder taking lithium develops excessive thirst and frequent urination over several weeks. Which investigation is particularly important?

choices.text: Renal function tests and serum electrolyte assessment
Routine visual acuity assessment only
Hearing assessment only
Skin allergy testing only

questions.rationale: Lithium can impair renal concentrating ability and cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, resulting in polyuria and polydipsia. Renal function and electrolyte assessment, particularly sodium, are important, alongside evaluation of hydration and serum lithium concentration.

distractor_rationales.B: Visual acuity testing does not evaluate lithium-associated renal complications.
distractor_rationales.C: Hearing assessment does not identify impaired renal concentrating ability.
distractor_rationales.D: Skin allergy testing is unrelated to the patient's urinary symptoms.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is attending to four patients. Which patient requires FIRST assessment?

choices.text: A patient with mild constipation after starting an antipsychotic
A patient with stable schizophrenia requesting a family meeting
A patient taking clozapine who develops fever, sore throat and profound weakness
A patient requesting information about healthy eating

questions.rationale: Fever, sore throat and profound weakness in a patient receiving clozapine may indicate severe neutropenia or agranulocytosis. Immediate assessment and urgent blood investigations are necessary because severe infection can develop rapidly.

distractor_rationales.A: Constipation requires assessment because severe complications can occur with clozapine, but the described symptoms in option C raise an immediate concern for serious infection.
distractor_rationales.B: A family meeting is a routine therapeutic intervention and is not an immediate emergency.
distractor_rationales.D: Dietary education is important but can be postponed.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving long-term antipsychotic medication develops repetitive tongue movements, lip smacking and involuntary facial grimacing. Which condition is MOST likely?

choices.text: Acute dystonia
Tardive dyskinesia
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Lithium toxicity

questions.rationale: Tardive dyskinesia is characterised by repetitive involuntary movements, particularly involving the tongue, lips, jaw and face, and is associated with prolonged exposure to dopamine receptor-blocking medications. Early recognition and clinical review are important because the condition may persist even after medication changes.

distractor_rationales.A: Acute dystonia generally presents with sudden sustained muscle contractions rather than persistent repetitive orofacial movements.
distractor_rationales.C: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is characterised by hyperthermia, rigidity and autonomic instability.
distractor_rationales.D: Lithium toxicity typically produces tremors, gastrointestinal symptoms and neurological impairment rather than classic tardive orofacial movements.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of the mental state examination?

choices.text: Appearance and behaviour
Speech and mood
Thought content and perception
Blood group and Rh factor

questions.rationale: The mental state examination systematically assesses current psychological functioning through domains such as appearance, behaviour, speech, mood, affect, thought, perception, cognition, insight and judgement. Blood group and Rh factor are laboratory-related medical information rather than components of the MSE.

distractor_rationales.A: Appearance and behaviour are standard MSE domains.
distractor_rationales.B: Speech and mood are essential areas of mental state assessment.
distractor_rationales.C: Thought content and perception are central components of the MSE.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse observes that a patient speaks rapidly, moves continuously, changes topics frequently and appears unusually cheerful and overconfident. Which mood-related condition should the nurse investigate?

choices.text: Mania
Apathy
Catatonia
Dementia only

questions.rationale: Elevated or irritable mood, increased activity, pressured speech and flight of ideas are characteristic features of mania. The nurse should further assess sleep, judgement, impulsivity, psychotic symptoms and potential risks to the patient and others.
